rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = | website = {{official URL}} }} {{Nottingham Forest FC sections}} '''Nottingham Forest Football Club''' is a professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[West Bridgford]], [[Nottinghamshire]], England. The club competes in the {{English football updater|NottingF}}, the top tier of [[English football league system|English football]]. Founded in 1865, Nottingham Forest have played their home games at the [[City Ground]] since 1898. The club has won two [[UEFA Champions League|European Cups]] (now the [[UEFA Champions League]]), making them one of six English clubs to have claimed the competition. Forest is the only team in Europe to have won the European Cup or Champions League more often than the domestic championship (one). Additionally, they have secured one [[UEFA Super Cup]], one [[List of English football champions|League title]], two [[FA Cup]]s, four [[Football League Cup|League Cup]]s, and one [[FA Community Shield|FA Charity Shield]]. The club has competed in the top two tiers of English football in all but five seasons since their admission to the Football League. Its most successful period came under the management of [[Brian Clough]] and [[Peter Taylor (footballer, born 1928)|Peter Taylor]] in the late 1970s and early 1980s, during which they achieved back-to-back European Cup triumphs in [[1978–79 European Cup|1979]] and [[1979–80 European Cup|1980]]. In Clough's final decade at the club, Forest won the [[1989 Football League Cup final|1989]] and [[1990 Football League Cup final|1990]] League Cups. They were also losing finalists in the [[1991 FA Cup final]] and [[1992 Football League Cup final|1992 League Cup final]], before relegation from the [[Premier League]] in [[1992–93 Premier League|1993]]. Upon their immediate return, Forest finished third in the Premier League in [[1994–95 Premier League|1995]], before suffering relegation again in [[1996–97 Premier League|1997]] and [[1998–99 Premier League|1999]]. The team returned to the Premier League by winning the [[2022 EFL Championship play-off final|play-offs]] in 2022. Forest's main rivalry is with [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]], with whom they contest the [[Derby County F.C.–Nottingham Forest F.C. rivalry|East Midlands derby]]. In 2007 the [[Brian Clough Trophy]] was founded, which has since then been given to the winner."}}
